summary: Tested whether home-page visits are tracked. Reproduced the bug: the fix E1 injected into inicio.html did NOT work in a real browser. The page's own CSP meta (default-src 'none' with no connect-src) blocked fetch('/api/track/access') ('Refused to connect because it violates the document's Content Security Policy'), so no request reached the backend. I fixed it by adding connect-src 'self' to the CSP meta in inicio.html. Retested: a fresh headless Chrome visit to / created an accesses doc (visitor_id v_mw28gy05_u3eja6qh, page '/'), a reload within 30 min was deduplicated, and the realtime feed showed 'Novo acesso desktop - Council Bluffs/IA'. Logged in to /donaspainel as donas: the ACESSOS card, funnel 'Acessos ao site' and 'Atividade em tempo real' all show the access. Backend track/access tests pass 6/6. Other admin dashboard routes return 200, and 401 without auth.

minor.issue: The 'access' events in db.events are not linked to the accesses doc (no visitor_id/access id). After deleting test accesses, their 'Novo acesso' events stay in the realtime feed, so the feed can show more items than the ACESSOS count.

ui_bugs.issue: ROOT CAUSE of the reported bug: CSP default-src 'none' without connect-src blocked the tracking fetch. FIXED by tester (added connect-src 'self').

issues: The same CSP also blocks /assets/mobile.css?v=3 (style-src 'unsafe-inline' has no 'self'), so mobile styles may not load. It also blocks Cloudflare beacon/challenge scripts. Consider adding 'self' to style-src (and script-src if external scripts are needed).

action_items: Keep the connect-src 'self' addition in /app/frontend/public/inicio.html CSP meta. If inicio.html is regenerated from SingleFile or the .bak, re-add it.
Add 'self' to style-src in the inicio.html CSP so /assets/mobile.css loads (currently blocked).
Optional: store visitor_id in access events so the realtime feed matches the accesses collection.
critical_code_review_comments: Any fetch-based tracker on a page with a restrictive CSP meta must check connect-src. E1's fix missed this, so the tracker failed silently (.catch swallowed the error).
The tracker swallows all errors silently. That is fine for production, but it hid this bug.
admin_routes.py is >2000 lines and should be split into modules.
seed_data_creation: pytest created 3 accesses (test_visitor_*); I deleted them by exact visitor_id. Their 3 'Novo acesso desktop' events remain in db.events. One real browser access (visitor_id v_mw28gy05_u3eja6qh, Council Bluffs) was kept as evidence. One pre-existing 'v_test_123' (curl-test) access from E1 also remains.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The tracker is inline JS at the end of inicio.html and posts {page, user_agent, extra:{visitor_id}}. Visits dedupe per visitor_id for 30 min. To check the browser flow, listen for console messages about CSP 'track/access' and query db.accesses by the visitor_id from localStorage. The browser_automation harness navigates to page_url before the script runs, so the first track request happens before your script starts.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: open / in Chrome. The console shows 'Connecting to .../api/track/access violates the following Content Security Policy directive: default-src none' and no request is sent. Cause: the SingleFile-saved inicio.html has a CSP meta with default-src 'none' and no connect-src, so fetch falls back to 'none'. Mitigation: add connect-src 'self' (applied, verified end-to-end).
